steps.headline: "Once upon a time": your script as a fairytale, for people already uneasy about big tech. Go ahead?
steps.today: Your own first half, nearly word for word, read by a quick British storybook voice over a drawn town whose identical windows each turn into a different youcoded.
steps.problem: It is the only take that tells the whole story of why this matters. It is also the one most likely to feel like a lecture if the voice or pictures are off.
steps.proposal: The full script is in the file. Pick what happens to this take.

options.label: Take it to voice and rough cut
pros: You see and hear it before deciding anything final.
It is your writing and your argument.
cons: The most work to get right: voice, drawing and timing all have to land.

options.label: Right idea, wrong words

cons: One more round of reading before anything moves.

steps.headline: "Make it mine": one person changing their youcoded by asking, six requests, no narrator. Go ahead?
steps.today: Six typed requests, each a different kind of thing: a look, their lights, a rearrangement, a tweak, a cute daily email, a frog game for a niece. The app changes each time.
steps.problem: It shows the customising, which no rival can show. Without care it could slide back into a feature tour.
steps.proposal: The full list is in the file. Pick what happens to this take.

cons: Every request shown has to be made for real once before I film it.

steps.headline: "Own everything": "you'll own nothing" crossed out to "everything", type only, 20 to 30 seconds. Go ahead?
steps.today: Words only: the phrase, the hand-drawn cross-out, then own your data, intelligence, software, everything. It doubles as a poster set.
steps.problem: It is the cheapest to make and the most shareable. On its own it never shows what youcoded is.

steps.headline: "Purple is the new orange": every AI model in one app, for people paying for one assistant. Go ahead?
steps.today: Your idea: looks that feel like each big assistant by colour and mood only, with the matching model named in the app's own picker, then a wheel of every model family.
steps.problem: It is the clearest reason for someone on one assistant to switch. It also leans on other companies' recognisable colours.
steps.proposal: I use no logos, names only as the real model picker shows them, and a "not affiliated" line. Before paying to place it, a lawyer should look.

options.label: Take it to voice and rough cut
pros: You see and hear it before deciding anything final.
Aims at the biggest audience: people already paying for one assistant.
cons: Needs three new looks made for real, and carries some legal risk if placed as a paid ad.

steps.headline: "Everyone's is different": five people, one wish each, then a screen full of different youcodeds. Go ahead?
steps.today: Five invented first names, each with one plain wish and a youcoded that looks nothing like the others. It ends on anything one person makes, everyone can use.
steps.problem: It is the only take that says youcoded is made by its users. The people are invented, which is weaker than real ones.

steps.page: Three things to settle before I draw anything
steps.intro: Each of these changes what you would see in every take.

steps.headline: In the fairytale, which wording about the big companies should I record first?
steps.today: The file has both. A is yours: "blinded by their own hubris" and "maximize shareholder value". B says they were "racing each other" and drops the motives.
steps.problem: You asked to see both before choosing. Recording both doubles the voice work for that take.
steps.proposal: Pick what I record for the voice checkpoint.

options.label: Record both
pros: You hear each one before deciding, as you asked.
cons: Twice the voice work for this take.

options.label: A only: their motives
pros: The sharpest, and exactly your words.
cons: Guesses at motives; some viewers will feel told off for what they use.

options.label: B only: the race
pros: Hard to argue with.
cons: Less bite.

steps.headline: How far may the app pictures in ads depart from the real app?
steps.today: The brand guide says ads use only recordings of the real app, and claim only what today's download does. You said cleaner, animated, made-up versions are fine because the app can make anything.
steps.problem: Made-up screens look better. But an ad showing something a viewer then cannot get is the thing advertising rules punish, and it is what would cost trust.
steps.proposal: Pick the rule. I change the brand guide to match your answer.

options.label: Redrawn, but made for real first
pros: Every example is made in youcoded once, then redrawn cleaner and animated.
Looks as good as invention, and every claim can be proven if challenged.
cons: Each example costs extra time to make for real first.

options.label: Anything the app could plausibly make
pros: Fastest, and no limit on what we show.
cons: If a shown example turns out not to work, the ad is misleading and we find out in public.

options.label: Real recordings only
pros: Nothing to defend.
cons: The plainer look you already found underwhelming.

steps.headline: "You'll own nothing and be happy" is tied online to a political conspiracy theory. Still use it?
steps.today: You want the phrase on posters with "nothing" crossed out. It began as a World Economic Forum video and is now a slogan in arguments about a supposed plot by global elites.
steps.problem: Most people will read it as a joke about subscriptions. Some will read youcoded as taking a political side, and a few news or ad outlets may refuse it.

options.label: Use it as you described
pros: Instantly recognisable, and the cross-out is a strong image.
cons: Some viewers attach politics to it.

options.label: Use "subscribe to everything, own nothing"
pros: Your own line from your script; no outside baggage.
cons: Less instantly recognisable.

options.label: Social posts only, not paid ads
pros: Keeps it where the joke is understood.
cons: Fewer people see the strongest image.
